meta.name: SoundKey Sound-Cue Library
meta.author: Krishita Sanjay Choksi
meta.description: The canonical mapping of SoundKey interface states and results to tones, patterns, spoken text, and haptics. This file is the single source of truth: the desktop simulator, the audio-demo generator, the on-device Flipper app, and the generated legend/gesture tables all read from it (the C app embeds a generated copy).
meta.design_notes: Frequencies are chosen to be comfortably within the Flipper piezo's usable range (~200-4000 Hz) and to be mutually distinguishable by ear. Categories use a rising musical scale (C5 major) so 'higher category = higher pitch' is learnable. Confirmation vs. error use a rising vs. falling two-note motif, a widely used screen-reader convention. Durations are in milliseconds.

envelope.note: A short attack/release removes clicks and mimics the softened square-ish tone of the on-device piezo without harsh edges.

tone_palette.comment: Named reference pitches so cues stay consistent and easy to retune in one place.

cues.label: Move to next/previous item
cues.purpose: A single soft tick emitted every time focus moves between menu items. Confirms the cursor moved without over-speaking.

cues.label: Edge of a list (no wrap)
cues.purpose: Played when the user tries to move past the first or last item. Tells them the list has an edge so they are not left guessing why nothing changed.

cues.label: Select / activate item
cues.purpose: Confirms an item was chosen and an action or submenu is opening.

cues.label: Go back / cancel
cues.purpose: Confirms the user backed out one level. Mirror image of select (falling instead of rising).

cues.label: Returned to home / main menu
cues.purpose: A distinct three-note home motif so the user always knows they are at the top level.

cues.label: Repeat last announcement
cues.purpose: A neutral acknowledgement that the last spoken/tonal announcement is being replayed.

cues.label: Action succeeded
cues.purpose: Rising two-note 'ta-da' motif. Universal 'done, good' confirmation.

cues.label: Action failed / not allowed
cues.purpose: Falling low buzz. Clearly distinct from success so the two are never confused.

cues.label: A running action started (e.g. scan begins)
cues.purpose: Marks the transition into an active/streaming mode. A wide octave leap UP -- an unmistakable 'we are going live' gesture, distinct from every navigation cue.

cues.label: A running action stopped
cues.purpose: Marks leaving an active mode. A wide octave leap DOWN, the mirror of action_start.

cues.label: Setting turned on
cues.purpose: Two quick equal high blips (flat contour) for boolean-on -- rhythmically distinct from the rising 'select' cue.

cues.label: Setting turned off
cues.purpose: Two quick equal low blips (flat contour) for boolean-off.

cues.label: Target found
cues.purpose: Bright, unmistakable double chirp announcing a positive result from a scan/read.

cues.label: Nothing found
cues.purpose: A single flat low tone. Deliberately unexciting so 'found' always stands out against it.

cues.label: Proximity / signal strength (geiger style)
cues.purpose: A stream of clicks whose RATE encodes closeness/strength: faster = closer/stronger. The signature sonification. Rate is computed at render time from a 0.0-1.0 level.

dynamic.note: rate = min + (max-min) * level^2, so the last approach accelerates sharply and gives fine discrimination when very close.

cues.label: Continuous value as pitch
cues.purpose: Maps a 0.0-1.0 value to pitch (higher value = higher pitch) for readouts like battery, volume, or a meter. Alternative to proximity for non-search values.

cues.label: Category as distinct tone
cues.purpose: Encodes a discrete category (1..6) as a note on a rising scale so categories are told apart by pitch. Used for e.g. signal type, tag class, or protocol family.

dynamic.note: category index (1-based) selects a note; index above the scale length wraps up an octave.

cues.label: Small count as beeps
cues.purpose: For small integer results (0-9), emits that many evenly spaced beeps so a count can be perceived without speech.

dynamic.note: counts above max fall back to spoken number.
